Hi Sarah — thanks for the checklist. I’ve answered each of the items inline below and attached our DR runbook and an RTO/RPO matrix for reference. Summary up top:

- Hosted inference: default cross-region routing with region failover; target RTO for new request routing is 90 seconds in a full-region outage with our standard routing policy. In practice we’ve observed cutover to the paired region in under 30s for most incidents. RPO for stateless model inference is effectively zero (no persisted per-request state).
- Customer-managed embeddings: we offer two replication options. Default async replication (low-latency, eventual) with typical RPO <= 60s; synchronous replication option for strict customers with RPO <= 5s (configurable at provisioning).
- Failover modes supported: active-passive (warm-standby), active-active with request-splitting, and DNS/LB-based cutover. Operational implications are below.

Detailed answers (by checklist row):
1) RTO / RPO commitments
- Control plane & routing: RTO target 90s; SLA exception process for sub-90s SLA is handled via Reserved Capacity (Dedicated) contract.
- Serving nodes (stateless): automated client retries + routing result in negligible client-visible RPO; in-flight RPCs may require client retry — we provide idempotency tokens to ease retries.
- Persistent stores (embeddings, metadata):
   * Async replication (default): RPO <= 60 seconds under normal operating load.
   * Sync replication (opt-in): RPO <= 5 seconds; suitable for regulated workloads.
- Audit logs & observability: all operational logs replicated to SIEM partners within 2 minutes; archived logs available for compliance for configured retention windows.

2) Failover approaches and what they mean
- Active-passive (warm-standby): secondary region has pre-warmed instances and replicated artifacts. On failover we flip routing; expected client-visible RTO ~ 2-5 minutes depending on DNS TTL and client retry behavior. Good tradeoff for cost-sensitive customers wanting predictable failover.
- Active-active: traffic split across regions with continuous replication of metadata. Offers near-zero RTO for new requests; in-flight requests may still be retried. This requires customer acceptance of eventual consistency for some caches unless you enable sync replication.
- DNS/LB cutover: for customers that control their DNS entries, TTLs of 30s or less plus health checks yield faster cutover; we also support DNS pre-warming.

3) Cache & KV behavior
- KV caches are transient and maintained per-region; we provide prefix-KV warming during cutover to minimize cold-start latency. For customer stateful caches we recommend persistent external stores with cross-region replication for RPO guarantees.

4) Evidence & rehearsals
- Attached: redwood_dr_runbook_v2.pdf and rto_rpo_matrix.xlsx.
- Last full regional failover rehearsal: 2028-05-11 (internal SRE-led, 2-hour window). Postmortem & checklist attached in the runbook.
- We can provide a scoped test report and a short recording of the runbook tabletop if needed for procurement review.

Next steps: If the answers look OK we suggest scheduling a 2-hour tabletop with your SRE and ours, followed by a limited failover rehearsal (non-production routing only) during a mutually agreed window. Grace and Neha — copying you to confirm SRE & CS coverage.

Connor O'Brien

Sarah — good questions. Answers below and I’ve attached the requested rehearsal postmortem excerpt.

- Sync replication availability & packaging:
   * Sync replication for persistent customer data (embeddings/metadata) is available for Hosted customers as an add-on; default Hosted plan uses async replication. For Dedicated/Private customers it is available as a configuration (included in many enterprise packages).
   * Cost: typical uplift for sync replication on Hosted is in the range of 12-18% of baseline storage/replication costs. Final pricing depends on retention and throughput profiles — we can provide a scoped estimate once we have your expected ingest and query rates.
- Model artifacts and weights sync: model binaries and weights are pushed to a global artifact registry (immutable hashes). We pre-stage artifacts to paired regions as part of deploy pipelines; integrity is verified using checksum and artifact signing. Recovery from a corrupted artifact is handled by a signed rollback to the last known-good hash; typical artifact redeploy to a region is under 10 minutes from detection when images are already in the registry.
- Rehearsal evidence & escalation list: attached excerpt contains the postmortem summary and the checklist used. For production failovers we provide a 24/7 escalation roster — I’ve included a redacted example in the runbook and will follow up with the full list under NDA or via your secure portal.

Proposed next steps:
1) Tabletop session — 60 minutes: review checklist and acceptance criteria (propose Tue 2028-09-05 11:00-12:00 PT).
2) Scoped rehearsal — 2 hours: non-prod routing cutover and verification (propose Fri 2028-09-08 02:00-04:00 PT; will be staff-only).

Grace / Neha — can you confirm availability for the proposed sessions and that SRE will run the rehearsal? Also we’ll need Legal on the escalation disclosure.

Connor
